title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 39 (Allotment of securities by company)

content.overview: Section 39 regulates allotment of securities offered to the public. No allotment shall be made unless the amount stated in the prospectus as the minimum amount has been subscribed and the sums payable on application for that amount have been paid to and received by the company by cheque or other instrument. Application money on every security shall not be less than five per cent of the nominal amount or such other percentage or amount as SEBI may specify by regulation. If the minimum is not subscribed and the application sum is not received within thirty days from issue of the prospectus (or such other SEBI-specified period), the amount received must be returned in the prescribed time and manner. A company having a share capital that makes any allotment of securities must file a return of allotment with the Registrar in the prescribed manner. Default under sub-section (3) or (4) attracts a penalty of one thousand rupees for each day of default or one lakh rupees, whichever is less.
content.glance: Minimum subscription and application money before public allotment; 5% (or SEBI) application-money floor; refund if minimum not met in time; return of allotment to Registrar; continuing daily penalty.
content.study:
Section 39 regulates allotment of securities offered to the public. It links public allotment to minimum subscription and receipt of the application money, prescribes the application-money floor subject to SEBI regulation, requires refund where the minimum is not achieved within the applicable period, and requires a return of allotment to be filed with the Registrar.

Statutory test
1. Public offer: the section applies to securities of a company offered to the public for subscription.
2. Minimum subscription: the amount stated in the prospectus as the minimum amount must have been subscribed before allotment.
3. Application money: the sums payable on application for the stated minimum amount must have been paid to and received by the company by cheque or other instrument.
4. Application-money floor: the amount payable on application on every security shall not be less than five per cent of the nominal amount of the security or such other percentage or amount as SEBI may specify by regulation.
5. Failure to achieve minimum: if the stated minimum amount has not been subscribed and the sum payable on application is not received within thirty days from the date of issue of the prospectus, or such other period as SEBI may specify, the amount received must be returned within such time and manner as may be prescribed.
6. Return of allotment: whenever a company having a share capital makes any allotment of securities, it shall file with the Registrar a return of allotment in such manner as may be prescribed.
7. Default consequence: for default under sub-section (3) or (4), the company and its officer in default are liable to a penalty of one thousand rupees for each day during which the default continues or one lakh rupees, whichever is less.

Application
A company receives applications for only 80% of its stated minimum subscription and proposes allotment. Identify section 39(1), test minimum subscription, consider the applicable period under section 39(3), explain the refund obligation, and separately address return-of-allotment filing under section 39(4).

Boundary
Section 39 governs public-offer allotment safeguards; section 42 governs private placement. Section 40 separately addresses recognised-stock-exchange permission and handling of public application monies.

sections.heading: Minimum subscription and application money
sections.body: No allotment of any securities of a company offered to the public for subscription shall be made unless the amount stated in the prospectus as the minimum amount has been subscribed and the sums payable on application for the amount so stated have been paid to and received by the company by cheque or other instrument.

sections.heading: Application-money floor
sections.body: The amount payable on application on every security shall not be less than five per cent of the nominal amount of the security or such other percentage or amount as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Board by making regulations in this behalf.

sections.heading: Refund if minimum not achieved
sections.body: If the stated minimum amount has not been subscribed and the sum payable on application is not received within a period of thirty days from the date of issue of the prospectus, or such other period as may be specified by SEBI, the amount received under sub-section (1) shall be returned within such time and manner as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Return of allotment
sections.body: Whenever a company having a share capital makes any allotment of securities, it shall file with the Registrar a return of allotment in such manner as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: In case of any default under sub-section (3) or sub-section (4), the company and its officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty, for each default, of one thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues or one lakh rupees, whichever is less.

examples.title: Minimum subscription required
examples.body: A public issue states a minimum subscription of ₹10 crore. Allotment cannot proceed merely because applications were received; the statutory minimum and required application money must first be satisfied.

examples.title: Refund obligation
examples.body: The stated minimum is not reached within the applicable period. The company must return application money in the prescribed manner and time.

examples.title: Return of allotment filing
examples.body: Allotment occurs but the prescribed return of allotment is not filed. The filing default attracts the statutory daily/maximum penalty under section 39(5).

hypotheticals.question: A company receives applications for only 80% of its stated minimum subscription and proposes allotment. Advise under section 39.
hypotheticals.analysis: Test section 39(1) minimum subscription and receipt of application money, the period under section 39(3), the refund obligation, and section 39(4) return of allotment separately. State only the statutory consequence.

distinctions.title: Section 39 vs section 40 / section 42
distinctions.left: Section 39 — public-offer allotment safeguards (minimum subscription, refund, return of allotment)
distinctions.right: Section 40 exchange permission and money ring-fence; section 42 private placement

rows.right: Different statutory trigger; do not merge regimes

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 39 as a rule for every private placement.
misconceptions.correction: Private placement is governed by section 42.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring SEBI power to vary the application-money floor.
misconceptions.correction: Section 39(2) allows SEBI to specify another percentage or amount by regulation.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing the refund trigger with exchange-permission requirements under section 40.
misconceptions.correction: Section 39(3) is about minimum subscription and application-money receipt; section 40 is about stock-exchange permission and segregation of application monies.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 39 be analysed on public-allotment facts?
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. ISSUE: Whether section 39 bars or conditions the proposed allotment.
II. RULE: Minimum subscription, application money by cheque/instrument, floor (5% or SEBI), refund period, return of allotment, daily/maximum penalty.
III. APPLICATION: Map each ingredient to the facts.
IV. CONCLUSION: State only the consequence supported by the current text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Facts; statutory ingredients of s. 39; distinction from ss. 40 and 42; precise statutory consequence under the current text.

examTips: Name section 39 and separate minimum subscription from return-of-allotment filing.
Do not apply section 39 to pure private placements.
State the penalty formula: ₹1,000 per day or ₹1 lakh, whichever is less.

Refund if minimum not met in 30 days (or SEBI period)

enhancement.definition: Section 39 links public allotment to minimum subscription and application money (by cheque or other instrument), sets an application-money floor of five per cent or SEBI-specified, requires refund if the minimum is not met within the applicable period, requires a return of allotment to the Registrar, and provides a continuing daily/maximum penalty for default under sub-sections (3) and (4).
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Securities offered to the public may not be allotted unless the prospectus minimum is subscribed and the application money is received; failure triggers refund; allotment requires a return to the Registrar.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 39(1) bars public allotment unless the prospectus minimum is subscribed and application sums are paid and received by cheque or other instrument. Section 39(2) sets the application-money floor at five per cent of nominal amount or such other percentage/amount as SEBI may specify. Section 39(3) requires return of amounts received if the minimum is not subscribed and application sum not received within thirty days (or SEBI period). Section 39(4) requires filing of a return of allotment with the Registrar. Section 39(5) imposes a penalty of one thousand rupees per day of default or one lakh rupees, whichever is less, for default under (3) or (4).
